readout_other: Scale for the Assessment of Negative Symptoms (SANS); Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS); Chinese Brief Cognitive Test (C-BCT: TMT-A, Symbol Coding, CPT, Digital Span); single-pulse TMS-elicited MEP of ipsilateral M1
direction_notes: The excitatory rTUS protocol to left DLPFC significantly decreased SANS and PANSS scores (negative symptom improvement), enhanced CPT cognitive performance, and increased ipsilateral M1 MEP amplitude (LTP-like plasticity) lasting up to 15 min post-stimulation.
safety_notes: Only 2 of 13 active-group patients reported difficulty falling asleep, resolved within 7 days; 3 sham-group patients reported dizziness throughout the intervention; no serious adverse events (SAEs) were reported.

timing.protocol_description: rTUS delivered via an immersion-type focused ultrasound transducer (focal length 3.8 cm, 500 kHz), driven by a custom-made TUS system, using pulsed ultrasound waves per the authors' previously published excitatory protocol for healthy humans; delivered on workdays for three consecutive weeks (15 sessions total) to the left DLPFC; ultrasound intensity was well below FDA guidelines. Numeric pulse parameters are shown only in a figure schematic (Fig. 1A), not stated in the text.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Then, 32 participants were randomly allocated, and 26 of them fulfilled the randomized controlled trial, with 13 patients in the active rTUS group and the other 13 patients in the sham group (Fig. S1).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: In conclusion, we demonstrate that 15 sessions of excitatory rTUS over the left DLPFC could alleviate the negative symptoms of schizophrenia patients and enhance the cognitive performance in CPT, suggesting the considerable potential of rTUS in clinical applications.
